description: How to turn a path written inside a released task file (drive task lists, pick task lists, job lists) into the release restore path of the file it names.

1. Absolute paths are used as they are. A relative path that starts with artifacts/ or assets/ is relative to the repository root. Any other relative path is joined to the root of the first relative_roots entry whose task_files glob ('*' stays within one folder) matches the task file's restore path, and normalised ('..' collapsed). Files matching task_files_exclude (metadata next to the task lists) are not task files.
2. The longest matching key of prefixes is replaced by its value (keys ending in '/' match folders, others one file). A repository-relative path without a matching key stays as it is.

3. If the result is not a released file but matches a copies rule, the task names a byte-identical renamed copy of a released pick route; recreate it from the 'of' path (the made_by command wrote them).

4. links: symlinks that the planners, the dataset builders and results/README.md go through; symlinks are never released. Recreate each from the repo root with: mkdir -p "$(dirname PATH)" && ln -s TARGET PATH (TARGET is relative to the link's folder). In the tracker by-arm views <route> runs over the 423 route ids of tracker_drive_folders (its run folder names without the __<arm> suffix); the v1 policy view is not a table arm and its drives are not released.

Every reference was resolved this way on 09-29; what does not resolve (collection inputs, arms outside the compact tables, one machine-specific file) is listed with reasons in the staging note path_remap_check.md.
